title: Re-instantiated phase-stop on the p = 11 paired cubes: conditional κ = 5.108294e-4
body:
## Conditional improvement

$$T(n)=O\big(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\big),\qquad \kappa=\frac{2554147}{5000000000}=\mathbf{5.108294}\times10^{-4}.$$

**Stacked on #152** (`ae9baba`, eumemic's paired cubes at p = 11 with the h = 21 bit word). Please review/merge that dependency first; its changes are not claimed here. The only files of this branch are `research/paired-cube-p11-tightened/` (README, verifier). The branch carries a single squashed commit on top of main because the push credential lacks workflow scope; relative to #152 the diff is exactly those two files.

## Change

One assembly instantiation constant is re-chosen. #152 inherits the merged #144 value `PHASE_STOP = 1/10^6`; the phase-stop beta is a free positive constant of the retained assembly (it enters only the `(1-beta)*AC - 10^-10` ceiling term and the 47 strict inequalities). #152's complex side binds (`AC = 5113520/10^10`), so the ceiling moves directly onto kappa at the grid:

| | phase-stop | kappa |
|---|---:|---:|
| #152 | 10^-6 | 5108289/10^10 |
| this branch | 10^-12 | **2554147/5*10^9** |

The same re-instantiation, at the same constant and for the same reason, is the move of #104 over #97 and of #135/#137/#138. No word, plan, row, bridge or interface changes; every inherited interface remains an assumption exactly as in #152.

## Verification

`python3 research/paired-cube-p11-tightened/verify.py` (stdlib, ~1 min): reproduces #152's published 5108289/10^10 exactly at the inherited constants, then rebinds `PHASE_STOP` to `10^-12` and reruns #152's own 47-constraint assembly: kappa = 2554147/5000000000 with the next 10^-10 grid point rejected, 47 strict constraints and 7 margins.

## Credits

- eumemic: #152 (p = 11 instance, h = 21 word) and #117, with Anthropic Claude assistance.
- icekylinx: #144/#130 (paired cubes, shared cores, assembly).
- Zhihao Chen (#97), Swapnil Jain (round-seven checkers), an664 (#128).
- Re-instantiation and this package: Abhinav Ramachandran with Hermes (Nous Research) assistance.

Conditional; no unconditional multiplication theorem is claimed.
